title: Finding Cosine and Tangent from Sine in Quadrant III
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Given that \sin x = -1/2 and x \in [\pi, 3\pi/2], find the exact values of \cos x and \tan x.

steps.title: Compute Cosine Squared from the Pythagorean Identity
steps.explanation: Substitute sin x = -1/2 into cos^2 x = 1 - sin^2 x to obtain 3/4.
steps.why: The identity sin^2 x + cos^2 x = 1 holds for all real x.

steps.title: Select the Negative Root for Quadrant III
steps.explanation: Because x is in Quadrant III, cos x is negative, so cos x = -sqrt(3)/2.
steps.why: Cosine is negative in the third quadrant.

steps.title: Compute Tangent
steps.explanation: Divide sin x = -1/2 by cos x = -sqrt(3)/2; the negative signs and denominators of 2 cancel, leaving 1/sqrt(3).
steps.why: Dividing two negative quantities in Quadrant III produces a positive tangent value.
